title: Connector description
description: One file per connector: what the agent sees (name, description, input schema, class, examples, named refusals) and the call behind it. Python and TypeScript are generated from it.

then.$comment: Without base_url or base_urls, every function must be handwritten.
A connector with access levels: every function declares the scopes it requires.

else.$comment: A connector without access levels: no function declares scopes.

dotted_path.description: Dotted path of a value in a JSON response, a list index as a number: credits.remaining, accounts.0.balance. Each segment is non-empty, without space.

timeout_s.description: A timeout in seconds: the connector's, or one function's. At most 300, the ceiling the host package of oto 2 runs.

account_mark.description: What a refusal reveals about the account, for the host to mark it until its next successful call: credential_rejected (the service refuses the key or the token of the account), quota_exhausted (its credits or plan quota are spent). Only what is declared marks: nothing marks by default.

body_condition.description: A condition on the JSON body of the response: the value at path (dotted, a list index as a number) equals one of the values. The entry applies only when it holds; under the same status, the next entry is tried.

argument_map.description: API-side name to input argument name. Each input argument goes to one place only.

constant_headers.description: Header name to a constant value. Never a secret: the file is public.

check.description: A check of the input before the call: when it fails, nothing is sent and the named refusal is returned.

kind.description: Over the items of a list argument, the sum of the first field equals the sum of the second; decimal strings are summed exactly.

expectation.description: A check of the response: when it fails, the named refusal is returned instead of the response.

kind.description: The value at path is present and is not null, nor an empty string, list or object.

url_template.description: An https URL without trailing slash. It may cite settings as {name}: a url setting (or a value read from the token) only at its head, where it stands for the scheme and the host; any other setting after https://. base_url may also cite the account identity (account_identity.name), after the host only.

urls_by_setting.description: One https URL per value of a choice setting: every choice has its URL.

additionalProperties.description: An https URL without trailing slash; it may cite the account identity as {name}, after the host only.

setting.description: A non-secret setting of an account, entered by whoever connects it: a region in a closed list, a free address, or a text checked by a pattern.

type.description: A value of a closed list.

default.description: One of the choices, taken when the account sets none.

type.description: A free text checked by pattern, such as the subdomain of a tenant.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression the value must match.

type.description: A free https address entered by an admin. At run time: https only, never a host that resolves to an internal address, no redirect followed.

handwritten.description: Code written by hand, referenced from the file. The rest of the entry stays declarative.

name.description: Stable identifier, first segment of the tools.

namespace.description: Prefix of the exposed tools, often equal to name.

api_version.description: Version of the third-party API, as the vendor names it.

base_url.description: Root of the call paths, possibly a template over settings and the account identity. base_url or base_urls is required unless every function is handwritten.

base_urls.description: Root of the call paths per value of a choice setting, such as a region.

settings.description: Non-secret settings of an account, beside its credential.

credential.description: Secret and non-secret fields of the credential supplied by the consumer: an account keeps every one. Required unless auth.kind is none or oauth2_user, which forbid it (the tokens of a consent are not credential fields).

holder.description: Who supplies the field. account: entered with the account. host: supplied by the host application, once for all its organisations; never stored with the account, shown or entered.

account_identity.description: Identifier of the account at a third party that hosts its users' accounts (a hosted messaging service), one value per account. Cited only by base_url, never by an argument, a call parameter or a constant: the agent never supplies it, the host writes it through a service that checks it with the third party.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression the identifier must match.

modes.description: Who may hold an account. Current vocabulary, to be aligned with organisation, team and person.

timeout_s.description: Timeout of one call, in seconds.

quota.description: Default quota on a platform key. Absent when the connector has no platform key. Shape still to be fixed.

query_arrays.description: Encoding of lists in the query string.

headers.description: Constant headers sent with every request of every function.

rate_limit.description: Highest rate the third party accepts, per credential: at most `requests` requests every `seconds` seconds.

probe.description: The function that checks a connection: a read function without required argument, never counted against a quota.

non_empty.description: Dotted paths that must be present and non-empty in its response.

balance.description: The balance of a paid account, read in the probe's response: a number at path, healthy at min or above; under min, absent or not a number, the probe is not healthy. The probe function then declares no cost: one never pays to learn whether one can pay.

path.description: Dotted path of the balance in the response.

min.description: Threshold: a balance under it is not healthy.

unit.description: What the balance counts, as the vendor names it: credits, requests, EUR.

errors.description: Error table shared by every function: the first entry whose status, and body condition when it has one, matches the response applies.

auth.description: Other keys depend on kind. Values naming a secret refer to connector.credential[].name; a URL template cites connector.settings[].name.

in.description: Where the key goes: a header, or the query of every call (masked in every log at run time).

name.description: Name of the header or of the query parameter.

prefix.description: Header only: text sent before the key.

token.description: Credential field sent as the bearer token.

oneOf.description: A person's consent (authorization code). The OAuth application (client id and secret) belongs to the host, or to the organization that sets its own: it is neither in this file nor in credential. The tokens the consent yields are not credential fields.

token_url.description: Token endpoint, called with a form body (authorization code, refresh, exchange).

scopes.description: Joined by spaces in the authorization request. Exclusive of access_levels: a connector without levels keeps scopes, and that is its full level.

scope_implies.description: With access_levels: a scope that covers others, as the provider defines it. Never a guessed rule: a broad scope covers a narrower one only when this file says so.

authorize_params.description: Constant parameters added to the authorization URL. Never one the host sets itself.

pkce.description: Proof key for code exchange, by SHA-256.

refresh.description: refresh_token: the refresh token grant; exchange: the current access token is exchanged for a new one; none: the token lives until it expires or is revoked, then the person consents again.

rotates.description: With refresh_token: each refresh returns a new refresh token that replaces the old one.

exchange.description: With exchange: the grant type, and the form parameter that carries the current access token.

expires_in_default.description: Lifetime in seconds of an access token whose response gives none.

identity.description: Who consented, read right after the consent to name the account, and the dotted path of a non-empty value in the response. Either a read function of the connector without required argument, or a full address read with GET outside base_url (a provider's common identity service), with the scopes it requires, which the consent asks for at every level.

url.description: Fixed https address, called with the access token and no argument.

scopes.description: Scopes this address requires, all of them.

from_token.description: Fields of the token response kept with the account, not secret, renewed at each token response, and citable in base_url like a setting.

client_auth.description: How the client id and secret reach the token endpoint: in the request body, or as HTTP Basic.

access_levels.description: Named access levels of a consent. full is required and filters nothing; any other name (read, support...) is a restricted level. Each level lists the scopes its consent asks for. The host picks one per organisation or team; a function is served at a level when each of its scopes is a scope of the level or implied by one (scope_implies).

scopes.description: Joined by spaces in the authorization request of this level.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema of the function input: a strict object.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema of one output record: a strict object, closed on the keys this connector promises — not every key is present on every call (a caller may narrow with its own `fields`/`embed`-style argument), but no key outside this set ever appears.

act.description: Whether the function commits or destroys (send, trash, archive, move): the host serves it as <connector>_act.<function>. Defaults from class: read false, write and sensitive true; a mere preparation, such as a draft, declares false. Never false on a sensitive function, never true on a read one.

description.description: What the agent reads, in English; at most 1000 characters.

timeout_s.description: Timeout of one call of this function, in seconds, in place of the connector's: longer or shorter, never equal to it. Each page of a paginated read is one call.

async.description: The function submits a job whose result is collected later by another function of the connector, collect, called with the job id read in the submission's response. With cost.settle, the real quantity is read in the collect's responses, within within_s, or, when the vendor's reference states that a job has no deadline, under no_deadline, until the billing service's own cap.

collect.description: The read function that collects the job: its state, and its result.

job_id.description: The job id: read at from in the submission's response, passed to the collect function as its argument to.

to.description: The only required argument of the collect function.

within_s.description: Delay of collection, in seconds after the submission: by then the job is done and its quantity readable. At most one day. With cost.settle, it or no_deadline is required.

no_deadline.description: The vendor's reference states that a job has no deadline: no delay of collection is declared, and a settled reservation lasts until its quantity is read or until the cap the billing service sets. Exclusive of within_s.

scopes.description: Only in a connector with access levels, where it is required: the scopes this function requires, all of them. It is served at a level when each is a scope of the level or implied by one. class stays: it says what the function does.

examples.description: Each input is validated against the function input.

refusals.description: Overrides or completes the connector error table.

checks.description: Checks of the input before the call; each names one of the function's refusals.

expect.description: Checks of the response; each names one of the function's refusals.

path.description: Relative to base_url, with {param} placeholders naming input arguments.

body.description: JSON body, whatever the method: a DELETE may carry one.

files.description: Multipart part name to the input argument that carries the id of a transit file of the caller. When present, the body is sent as multipart/form-data: each body entry and body constant becomes a text part, each file a part with the file's own name and type. The host reads the file under the caller's identity and consumes it after a successful send.

constants.description: Values sent with every call of this function. They are not arguments: the agent neither sees nor sets them.

encode.description: Argument name to its encoding before it is placed: json serialises a structured argument into one string.

pagination.description: When present, all_pages and max_pages are added to the served input schema.

request_param.description: Input argument carrying the cursor or page number.

next.description: Dotted path of the next cursor or page number in the response.

total.description: Dotted path of the total count in the response.

more.description: Dotted path of a boolean in the response: false means this page is the last, whatever next holds.

schema.description: Shape of one record, after items/strip/projection are applied.

items.description: Dotted path of the list in the response.

cost.description: What a call costs. Before the call, its worst case from the arguments: one per request sent (request, page: each page of a paginated read is a request), or, per item, the size of the items argument times the size of the times argument, or the sum over the items of the weights of the values each lists (weights). After the call, settle reads the real quantity in the response. Both count the same unit.

items.description: per: item only, required there: the list argument each element of which counts once. Required in the input, at least one element.

times.description: per: item only: another list argument whose size multiplies the count of items. Required in the input, at least one element.

weights.description: per: item only, exclusive of times: each element of items counts the sum of the weights of the values it lists in its own field, a list of values each of which has an integer weight of one or more in unit. The field is required in each element, a list of at least one element, unique values, every allowed value (its enum) weighted and nothing else.

field.description: The list field of each element of items that holds the values.

values.description: Weight of each allowed value, in unit: an integer of one or more.

unit.description: What the quantity counts, as the vendor names it: credits, contacts, fields. Required per item or with settle; absent, requests (per: request) or pages (per: page).

settle.description: The real quantity of the call, read to settle it: a finite JSON number of zero or more at path, in unit, in the response of the call, or of its collect function when it is asynchronous. Not on a paginated function.

summary.description: Template shown before execution, with {param} placeholders.

allOf.$comment: call and handwritten are exclusive; one of them is required.
An asynchronous function whose cost is settled says within how long its quantity is collected, or that the vendor sets no deadline.

mode.description: Overrides the instance default for this connector.

tool.description: Name of the single tool in per_connector mode; namespace otherwise.
